ShortDescription.Value: Outline any perimeter with existing roads and fill it with streets in one click: grid, loops, Barcelona-style superblocks or concentric rings. 42 languages.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Grid Road Generator
Click existing road nodes to outline any perimeter — rectangle, L-shape, rotated, curved or irregular (double-click a node to select the whole block automatically) — pick a pattern, then press **Generate** to fill it with connected streets. Generated streets join the perimeter roads and any road already crossing the area.
## Four patterns **Grid** — the classic street grid, oriented on the perimeter's longest edge. - Fit to area (rows/columns spread evenly) or fixed spacing in meters - Columns, rows, spacing and extra angle - Cul-de-sac mode: turn columns, rows or both into dead ends, with depth, frequency, staggering and a turnaround circle (automatic or manual size, asphalt, grass or tree-lined) - Avenue: promote one column and/or one row to an avenue with its own road type; where both cross, a real roundabout island is placed
**Loop** — a sparse grid of collector roads (200–400 m apart) dividing the area into blocks, each served by an internal loop street, with optional cul-de-sac branches.
**Superblock** — inspired by Barcelona's superilles: the area is divided into buildable zones (100–400 m, adjusted to fill the area exactly) separated by pedestrian streets. Every third line is a collector road; on a small selection the perimeter road itself plays that role. Pedestrian streets connect to the collectors and to the perimeter road.
**Concentric** — rings that copy the shape of the perimeter, one inside the other. - 1 to 10 layers; the slider stops at the number of rings that fit the selected shape (at least 40 m between rings, even in the narrowest part) - Every ring goes around the whole shape: tighter in narrow parts, wider in wide ones — no splitting, no pointed tips - Straight sides stay straight, sharp corners stay sharp, curves stay smooth - 2 to 12 radial connections spread around the perimeter, linking every ring to the outside road
## Networks and upgrades (Loop, Superblock, Concentric) - Choose a separate road for collectors, local streets and pedestrian paths - Automatic upgrades applied at build time: median trees or grass, roadside trees, bike lanes, wide sidewalks (left/right)
## Preview - A lightweight line sketch shows the result and updates live while you drag any slider, colored by road type (collector, local street, pedestrian) - The real in-game preview is only built when you press Generate, where it is validated like any road placement - If placement is blocked (collision, slope…), the real preview stays visible with a clear message, so you can see and fix the conflict - Optional: **Options > Mods > Grid Road Generator > General > Automatically remove colliding roads** removes the generated pieces in conflict and retries (off by default, as it can leave gaps in the pattern)
## Interface - **Reset values** button next to the pattern selector: restores the default values of every pattern - Panel styled like the game's own panels: dark title bar with icon and close button, body that follows **Options > Interface > Transparency** and your interface style - Draggable panel, collapsible sections, road picker with search and categories - View toggles: underground networks, zone grid and normally-invisible networks - Follow terrain, or keep the generated streets flat at the perimeter's average elevation
## Compatibility - **[Anarchy](https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/74604/Windows)** by **yenyang** (optional): if installed, a toggle appears in the panel header, synced with Anarchy's own button and shortcut. No hard dependency.
## Keybindings (Options > Mods > Grid Road Generator) - **Ctrl+G**: toggle the tool - **Enter**: generate - **Left click**: add/remove a node · **Double-click** the first node: select the whole perimeter · **Right click**: remove the last node · **Escape**: clear the selection
All other settings live in the in-game panel and persist between sessions.
## Languages **42 languages**: - **12 official game languages**: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional) - **30 community languages**, shown when a language mod adds them to the game (e.g. I18N Everywhere or a language pack): Portuguese (Portugal), Ukrainian, Thai, Vietnamese, Dutch, Arabic, Czech, Danish, Persian, Finnish, Filipino, Greek, Hindi, Croatian, Hungarian, Indonesian, Norwegian, Romanian, Swedish, Turkish, Catalan, Galician, Basque, Occitan, Welsh, West Frisian, Breton, Scots, Sardinian, Abkhaz
## Credits Node-selection, tooltip and UI architecture patterns adapted from [CS2-NetworkTools](https://github.com/lucarager/CS2-NetworkTools) by Luca Rager, under the MIT license. Thank you!
Publish.ChangeLog:
**0.3.1 - Concentric fixes and new options**
Concentric: - No more collisions where connections meet the rings: connections always join a ring at an open angle, never inside a fold, and no tiny road pieces are left next to junctions - Connections are continuous lines from the perimeter to the centre (no more staggered pieces), and they reach the centre even through narrow parts of the shape - Rings keep the shape of the perimeter again instead of becoming rounder towards the centre, with pointed tips smoothly rounded - Perimeters that follow curved roads are cleaned of tiny back-and-forth kinks where two roads join (all patterns) - Faster generation when changing layers and connections
New options: - Options > Mods > Grid Road Generator > General: "Automatically remove colliding roads" (off by default). When Generate is refused because of a collision, the generated pieces in conflict are removed and generation is retried - "Reset values" button in the panel, next to the pattern selector: restores the default values of every pattern (keeps the chosen pattern, networks, upgrades and view)
Fixes: - Closing the panel while the real preview was shown caused a critical error - When Generate is refused, the log now lists where the game found the collision
